questions.question: What are the two engineering benefits that the model's statelessness buys?
options: Retries are safe and concurrency is safe
Automatic context memory and automatic follow-up
No training required and no prompting required
questions.explanation: See the "The model is a single call" section: statelessness buys two engineering benefits — retries are safe (a failed call can be resent as-is) and concurrency is safe (two requests know nothing of each other).

questions.question: When does the agent loop exit?
options: When the maximum context window is reached
When the model's output is a final answer rather than an action request
When the user closes the window
When the tool list is emptied
questions.explanation: See the "Give the model a loop" section: the loop's exit condition is decided by the model's output — when it produces a final answer instead of an action request, the loop ends.

questions.question: Why does the body recommend preferring a workflow over a loop for a task with a fixed path?
options: Every step waits for the model's on-the-spot decision, adding an extra call's latency and cost plus the freedom to take a wrong turn
Loops only work for multi-agent systems
questions.explanation: See the "Give the model a loop" section: wrapping a loop around a task whose path is fixed is pure overhead — every step waits for the model's decision, costing an extra call while adding the freedom to take a wrong turn.
